doc.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023

title: Advice to students: passion
summary: Radke tells students to follow their passion and drop the ego, and praises Hillsdale's students.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: This has been a fascinating conversation and I’d like to wrap up with the fact that you have this terrific relationship with Hillsdale College. It’s wonderful to hear that you’re working with the trumpet students. Do you have any words of wisdom that you share with them about trying to — if they express this interest of —

That’s a — you know the music business is a tough thing today as you know. And I think, what I tell anybody, it’s all passion. And I think if you’re passionate about what you want to do, and you want to be a trumpet player then follow that passion. And you know if you visualize, if you want to look at — look what I visualized. And I have a great wife, she’s just great, and I have great children and grandchildren and great grandchildren, and Cocoa Puff, our dog. You know just, and great friends. You know if you’re a positive person and leave your ego at the stage door canteen. I love once again referring back to Bobby Shew. He says forget your ego man. As you get older what’s — ego is, that’s for children. And I think for students if they want to pursue that go for it. Have your passion. You have to have the passion. You have to have the drive. You have to want it bad enough. And then you go for it. And that’s what I’d say. This place, Hillsdale College, I’ve been coming here for five or six years. I don’t know if you’ve had time just to sit around and observe. The other day I was sitting on the bench up there and then I went to the dining room and just sitting there watching students. This is a positive, happy place. Everybody smiles, everybody is extremely polite, everybody is friendly, and it’s just a positive place to be. And I was watching, you know, just people walking down the street, laughing, talking, arms around each other, shaking hands. In the cafeteria sit down with a couple of other professors and they engaged in doing, you know very important conversations. It’s just a positive place. And I think that a student that goes here who is very privileged to do so, to have the opportunity to come and get this
education at this institution, they’re going to leave here with a positive driving force and driving attitude to do what they want to do. I really feel that.
